issue_context.title: Command Line sensor value_template using value_json returning unknown as state
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When using value_json in the value_template for a command line sensor which calls a script outputting JSON, the state of that sensor is always "unknown", although attributes populated via json_attributes are poplualted as expected.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.4.0b2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2023.3.4

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Command Line Sensor

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor.command_line/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
- platform: command_line
  name: "Command Line Test"
  command: python3 /config/command_line_scripts/command_line_test.py
  scan_interval: 3600
  value_template: >-
    {{ value_json.data_items | length }}
  json_attributes:
    - data_items
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

Here is the Python script used for the test sensor:

```Python
import json

data = {"data_items": [{"name":"item1"},{"name":"item2"}] }

print(json.dumps(data))
```
comments:
After further testing of this it looks like this issue is not actually anything to do with **value_json**, it looks like **value_template** is being complete ignored if **json_attributes** is present. Even a hardcode string is ignored

For example:

```YAML
- platform: command_line
  name: "Command Line Test"
  command: python3 /config/command_line_scripts/command_line_test.py
  scan_interval: 3600
  value_template: "OK"
  json_attributes:
    - data_items
```
Gives a state of "unknown" with the attributes set.

While removing the **json_attributes** option like this:

```YAML
- platform: command_line
  name: "Command Line Test"
  command: python3 /config/command_line_scripts/command_line_test.py
  scan_interval: 3600
  value_template: "OK"
```

Gives the state as "OK" without the attributes

The value_template is also used to render non JSON output to a sensor state value. Your PR attached could (with some changes) also deliver JSON output though the `value_template`. A new feature could be that if an attribute is parsed with the name `state` to set the sensor state.

> It should still work for either JSON or non-JSON values.

But when json_attributes is used it is assumable that value is a dict. With your PR that would be assigned if value_template is `None`. Better is to use the value_template to render before checking the json and read the value from attribute `state` if json_attributes is set. That last part should be a separate PR. But when value_template is `None` and json_attributes is set `value` should be `unknown`

Hi Steven, I was thinking about something like this:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/compare/dev...jbouwh:commandline-sensor?expand=1

That would allow to create JSON from a non JSON output and still allow to set a state.

I can confirm that the behavior has changed in 2023.4. I have a lot of sensors which use command line with JSON output and I use the value_template to make the make the main JSON attribute the sensor value. All broken now…

The code example from the Home Assistant documentation doesn’t work anymore. 

```python
# Example configuration.yaml entry
sensor:
  - platform: command_line
    name: JSON time
    json_attributes:
      - date
      - milliseconds_since_epoch
    command: "python3 /home/pi/.homeassistant/scripts/datetime.py"
    value_template: "{{ value_json.time }}"
``` 

this sensor will now have value “unknown”. Was this an on purpose change (so documentation should be changed) or is it a bug?
It seems to me this is a bug as the documentation shows an example they can be used together.
I agree this is a bug, I was hoping to implement some command line sensors as @lancer73  has done and was expecting to set the default value for the sensor to be one of the JSON values returned.

review_comments:
With this change, if no value is set and json_attributes are used the json payload is assigned as a state.
So make sure that both value_template and json_attributes are not set before assigning the value to the sensor state.

May be we should use the value_template to parse `value` before it tries to serialize the JSON. In that case we could map the `state` attribute the the sensor state. This makes it possible to parse values from command output that is not JSON.

IMO You create a new issue with the else at L148-L149.
We should not set the native value if `json_attributes` is set and a dict is expected, and `value_template` is not set.
I was thinking of something like: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/compare/dev...jbouwh:commandline-sensor?expand=1.

It looks like that change would result in the state being unknown if the JSON attributes don't include **state**, even if there is a value_template defined.

Would doing this be OK as a compromise?

```Python
self._attr_native_value = (
      json_dict[CONF_STATE] if CONF_STATE in json_dict else value
)
```

So that it would default to the value from rendering value_template.

> Would doing this be OK as a compromise?

If `json_attributes` is set value is a assumed to be a `dict`. We do not want to write that as a state too. When a `value_template`  is set, then the state could be rendered to a simple value (only when json_attributes is not set). My suggesting is to make the `value_template` useful for rendering a non json output to a json output so that `json_attributes` can be used to in that case.

I'm not sure that it makes sense to use value_template to render a non-JSON output to JSON, as the main function of it is to render to the output to a simple value. For example, one of my sensors calls a script which returns multiple values in an array in a JSON object (e.g. `{"names":["Test1","Test2"]}`.
the value_template is used so the latest value is the state of the sensor, and the json_attributes has an attribute returning all the versions.

Making this change would require users to change the scripts so that the JSON they return would include a "state" attribute, if they are using json_attributes and don't want the value of their sensor to be "unknown".

I've implemented the original suggestion now, so if there is no value_template, but json_attributes are used the state will be None (to avoid the state being populated with the raw JSON data). I think for now that is the simplest thing to do and it still resolves the original issue.

```suggestion
        elif self._value_template is not None:
```

If we use elif we know json attributes is None, so we just can assign the rendered template, and return.
The the case that this left is where we just assign the value. We do not need an if for that.

At L150

```python
            ...
        else:
            self._attr_native_value = value
 ```

becomes

```python
            ...
            return
        self._attr_native_value = value
 ```
I think that would bring back the original issue where value_template would only be used if json_attributes isn't, but the two options should be usable together.
Sorry, i'll have a better look at it
